text: Be not hard, like the bones of men, nor soft as a sponge.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: Be not over sweet, lest they eat thee up, nor over bitter, lest thy friends run away from thee.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: If thou hast a wound on thy foot, step not forth firmly.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: When a man distinguishes himself, worry him not; if a mishap occur to him, rejoice not over it.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: Relate to no one what thou hearest, and reveal to no one what thou seest.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: A liar findeth sympathy at first, but at the last he is despised and abused.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: If fierce anger seize thee, say not a word, lest thou be called senseless.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: Take up no quarrel with a man stronger than thyself; thou canst not know how he will pounce on thee.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: If thy house be too high, make the walls lower, and then walk in.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: Keep a sweet tongue and open thy mouth to speak what is good.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: Be not fain to trample on thy neighbour, lest the like happen to thyself.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: Prove thy friend first with bread and wine, then may he be admitted to something better.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: It is better to listen to a wise man when he is drunk than to a noodle when he is sober.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: A friend who dwells near thee is better than a brother far off.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: It is better for thee to be robbed than to rob thyself.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: If thou say a good word for thy friend before the judge, thou hast snatched a lamb out of the jaws of the lion.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: If thou hast wealth, do not allow thyself to be tormented by hunger or thirst.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: If any one is punished for a fault, say not that he is punished without reason, lest thou incur the same penalty.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: If thou hast no horse of thine own, ride not on a strange one; if it becomes lame, thou wilt be laughed at.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: If thou hast no bodily hunger, eat not bread, lest thou appear greedy.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: I have carried salt and have removed lead; and I have not seen anything heavier than that a man should pay a debt that he did not borrow.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: The man who despises the law goes towards his fall, but the just man will rise higher.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: Judge uprightly and thou wilt be honoured in thine old age.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: If thou drink wine, speak little.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: Venture not on the road with a man who will not accept advice, and sit not down at the same table with a deceiver.
source: Story of Ahikar (sayings of Ahikar, composite versions)
era: sage of the 7th c. BCE (versions later)
translator: F. C. Conybeare, J. R. Harris, A. S. Lewis, 1913

text: All men are influenced by class-feelings, and there are few who are intelligent.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896

text: Few men are utterly bad.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896

text: In this world, few are born with knowledge: wisdom is the product of earnest meditation.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896

text: Therefore did the wise sovereigns of antiquity seek the man to fill the office, and not the office for the sake of the man.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896

text: Good faith is the foundation of right.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896

text: Let us cease from wrath, and refrain from angry looks.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896

text: Their right is our wrong, and our right is their wrong.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896

text: For we are all, one with another, wise and foolish, like a ring which has no end.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896

text: Chastise that which is evil and encourage that which is good.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896

text: In a country there are not two lords; the people have not two masters.
source: Prince Shotoku, Seventeen-Article Constitution (Nihongi)
era: 604 CE
translator: W. G. Aston, 1896
